english.title: Possess anatomical specimens away from licensed premises - Human Tissue Act 2004
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed anatomical specimen, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SPECIMEN..), when not on premises in respect of which an anatomy licence issued under Schedule 3 of the Human Tissue Act 2004 was in force
english.legislation: Contrary to section 30(1) and (7) of the Human Tissue Act 2004.

english.notes:
(i)Section 30(2) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides that the offence does not apply where
(a) the specimen has come from premises in respect of which a storage licence is in force, AND
(b) the person is authorised in writing by the designated individual to have possession of the specimen, AND
has possession of the specimen only for a purpose for which he is authorised to have possession of it.
(ii)Section 30(3) of the Act provides that the offence does not apply where the person has possession of the specimen only for the purpose of transporting it to premises in respect of which a storage licence is in force, OR where the specimen is to be used for the purpose of education, training or research.
(iii)Section 30(4) of the Act provides that the offence does not apply where the person reasonably believes that what he has possession of is not a former anatomical specimen OR that the specimen is on premises in respect of which a storage licence is in force OR that any of subsection (2) to (4) applies.
(iv)Section 30(8) of the Act provides that anatomy licence means a licence authorising the carrying-out of anatomical examination OR the storage of anatomical specimens and storage licence means a licence authorising the storage of anatomical specimens.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
